title: Filename uniqueness fixed; audit_id payload identity is unchanged legacy and deferred
body: F001 changes the audit envelope FILENAME to `{agent}-{role}-{feature_id}-i{n}.json`. The payload's `audit_id` field stays `{plan_id}#{agent}#{iteration}` per its existing definition (set in F005a-1 of plan 2026-04-19-001 and inherited by audit.schema.json). Two features within the same plan can therefore still produce envelopes whose payload `audit_id` strings collide (e.g., F001 round 0 and F002 round 0 of plan 2026-05-02-002 both serialize as `2026-05-02-002#claude#0`). Why this is acceptable for v1: (a) the bug this plan fixes is FILE OVERWRITE — F001's envelope being clobbered on disk by F002's write — and changing the filename is a complete fix for that; (b) downstream consumers that index on payload audit_id (mostly transcript.md and signoff_writer) currently treat each plan as single-feature-at-a-time, so the payload collision is not observable to them today; (c) expanding `audit_id` to embed feature_id would be a schema bump (`agent-conventions/schemas/v1.0/audit.schema.json` audit_id format), which is explicitly out of scope (mirrors D006 of plan 2026-05-01-005). Why we don't fix payload identity now: speculatively expanding identity surface invites the same scope-creep that motivated D006. If a future consumer needs unambiguous per-feature audit identity (e.g., a multi-feature event timeline), the identity-expansion plan can use feature_id as already-validated input from F001 of this plan. How to apply: any future plan that needs payload-level disambiguation between same-plan features should reference this D-entry in its motivation and propose the schema bump explicitly (separate plan, not bundled). Until then, treat payload audit_id collision within a plan as a known legacy property — filename uniqueness from F001 of this plan is the operative anti-collision contract.

title: feature_id sanitization at write boundary — `^F\d{3}$` regex, no raw strings in paths
body: F001's `audit_writer.write` validates the new `feature_id` kwarg against `^F\d{3}$` (the regex used by `agent-conventions/schemas/v1.0/features.schema.json` for feature ids — kept identical, no platform fork). On mismatch, raises `ValueError` BEFORE creating audit_dir or writing any bytes (mirrors plan 005 F002 acceptance #5 — no-partial-artifact). Rejected inputs: `None`, `''` (empty), `'F1'` (too short), `'feat-1'` (wrong shape), `'F001/../escape'` (path traversal). Why strict at the writer boundary: (a) feature_id is operator-supplied via plan_id selection at dispatch time, but flows through python kwargs without separate validation — without sanitization a path-traversal arg could write outside `audit/`; (b) the regex is already the authoritative feature_id shape from agent-conventions, so adding the same check at the writer is single-source-of-truth, not duplicated rules; (c) failing fast at the writer matches the pattern already established by D004 of plan 2026-05-01-005 (hard-fail on invalid struct, no silent fallback). How to apply: any future writer-side identifier (signoff filename keyed by something other than plan_id, transcript shard names, etc.) should validate at the boundary against the agent-conventions schema regex, not invent a parallel pattern.

title: F001 close-out — direct path (no volley) for the audit-filename feature_id change
body: F001 shipped via TDD red→green direct path — no volley dispatched. Operator-approved on 2026-05-02. Rationale: the feature is a small, mechanical writer/callsite/test change (single audit_writer.write mutation, 2 supervisor callsite updates, 1 transcript docstring update, 16+1+2 test-side mechanical updates, 22 new tests covering all 12 acceptance clauses). Acceptance was heavily disambiguated at lock time across D001 (payload audit_id identity deferral) + D002 (feature_id boundary-validation rationale, schema as single source of truth). No design space, no interpretive lookup, no severity classification involved. Per the failure-taxonomy memory captured during plan 005's F002 close-out, additional volleys on saturated, well-bounded surfaces produce interpretive_disagreement-class findings rather than feature_defect-class — testing review-loop instability rather than implementation. Direct path delivered: audit_writer.write(audit, plan_dir, *, feature_id) with `^F\d{3}$` validation; both production callsites (dispatch_single_agent line 595, dispatch_volley line 1342) thread feature_id; transcript.py docstring updated; 22 tests in test_audit_filename_feature_id.py covering filename pattern, iteration sequencing, collision-free F001+F002, parametrized negative cases (13 invalid inputs), regex drift detector against features.schema.json $defs.feature, old-pattern envelope readability, structural no-glob proof, both dispatch paths via scripted executors. Test/lint state at close-out: 22/22 F001 targeted tests pass, 469 + 6 skipped full orchestrate suite (was 447 → +22), ruff clean, sanitization clean (551 files). No agent retraining, no schema bump, no historical envelope rename — just the writer/callsite/test mechanical change. How to apply: future small, mechanical platform patches with locked acceptance and prior-context disambiguation should follow this direct-path pattern; the volley failure-taxonomy memory documents the trigger conditions. Plan 002 fully closed after this commit (single-feature plan).

Plan 005's status-flip memo at `1e06fc3` already recorded the expected resolution path (`Audit-envelope filename collision ... Deferred to Plan 2026-05-02-002 (still active). NOT solved by this plan.`). Now closes here at owning-plan level — without retroactively modifying Plan 005's memo.
